label: SYNTHETIC. Made up practice lines, not real customers.
how_to_use: Each line is something a prospect might say. 'answer' is the number of the answer that fits it best. 'direct' lines name the objection; 'hidden' lines only hint at it.

items.text: Salesforce just launched an AI agent for this. Why wouldn't I go with them?
My brother in law keeps forwarding me articles about Salesforce doing this with AI. He thinks I'd be mad to pay anyone.
HubSpot's thing is a dollar a lead. Your number looks huge next to that.
I did the maths on a dollar per lead and your monthly fee buys me a lot of leads.
Clay is what all the growth people use. Isn't that the cheaper route?
A guy in my founder group built his whole outbound in Clay and pays almost nothing.
I'm technical enough. I'll just wire up a tool myself.
Give me a couple of weekends and a YouTube tutorial and I reckon I'm there.
Surely the software is cheaper than an agency.
What does Salesforce charge for that agent? I'm guessing it's a fraction of you.
I read that the agent handles the deal for weeks. So what's left to do?
From the launch video it looked like you just switch it on and it sells.
Our admin could just run this on the side.
Jo has some slow afternoons, we could give her a login and let her get on with it.
I'd prefer to hire someone junior and train them up.
There's a graduate I know who needs a job. Wouldn't she do the same thing for less?
Can't I do all this with a ChatGPT subscription?
I asked Claude to write me a cold email last night and honestly it was pretty good.
If AI writes it, what's your actual job here?
So you press a button and I pay you monthly for that?
You're very small. What if you disappear?
Nobody ever got fired for buying from the biggest name, you know.
Will you commit to a set number of meetings every month?
I'd sign today if you can tell me I'll definitely get 10 calls.
I hate those AI emails and I don't want to send them.
My whole business runs on referrals and being known as the decent ones in town.
What if the AI invents something about my company?
Last week a chatbot told me a shop was open on Sunday and it wasn't, so you can see why I'm nervous.
Who else in my line of work have you done this for?
Sounds nice, but everyone's got a slide with a graph going up.
They've got 240 million contacts. What have you got?
Surely a list that big has everyone I'd ever want to sell to.
If we part ways, what happens to all the leads?
My last marketing company held my website hostage for 2 months.
We just use a spreadsheet. Shouldn't we get a CRM first?
Honestly it's all in my inbox and my head at the moment. Is that embarrassing?
Is this allowed? You're not scraping LinkedIn are you?
A mate of mine got his LinkedIn account restricted using one of these tools.
Are you putting my customer list into an AI model?
I signed an NDA with my biggest customer, so I'm a bit twitchy about where this goes.
We're already paying for HubSpot. Why pay for this as well?
My finance lead will ask why this isn't covered by the software we've already got.
We'll be moving to Salesforce at some point, so it seems wasteful to start here.
Our investor keeps saying we should get on a proper system before we do anything else.
Won't AI make this whole service pointless next year?
I'd feel daft signing up for something a robot will do for free by summer.
Let's hold off until the Salesforce agent is out and see what it's like.
No rush on our side. Things are moving so fast, let's check back in a couple of months.
We already tried one of these AI SDR products and it flopped.
We paid for 6 months of something similar and all we got was angry replies.
